expectations.text: Identifies the tension or contradiction between 'stateless' and 'WebSocket state persistence'
expectations.evidence: Explicit contradiction table: 'Stateless — no server-side session storage' vs 'WebSocket connections must persist user state'. States: 'These two constraints are mutually exclusive as written.'

expectations.text: Does NOT silently pick one interpretation and plan around it without flagging the conflict
expectations.evidence: Explicitly stops: 'I cannot write a sound implementation plan until the contradiction is resolved.' No plan file generated.

expectations.text: Presents design options for resolving the conflict (e.g., external state store, token-based state, etc.)
expectations.evidence: Three interpretations: (a) Stateless REST only, WS allowed state, (b) No external session store but in-memory OK, (c) Stateless auth per message (JWT). Plus 5 clarifying questions.

expectations.text: Asks for user input on how to resolve the conflict BEFORE writing a full plan
expectations.evidence: Ends with: 'Please clarify which definition of stateless applies and what user state means in this context, and I will proceed immediately to a full plan.'
